newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW -- U.S. April PPI falls 0.6 percent.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW -- U.S. April PPI falls 0.6 percent.

text.p: Following are comments from U.S. economists after the Labor Department said the Producer Price Index (PPI) fell 0.6 percent in April. Excluding food and energy, the index was down 0.1 percent.
Economists had expected overall PPI to stay unchanged. The core rate was seen rising 0.1 percent.
PHILIP BRAVERMAN, CHIEF ECONOMIST, DKB SECURITIES: "I think we're experiencing some benefits of the facts that oil prices had run up last year and are now on the process of falling."
"But there is clearly, in a lot of areas, a deflationary element and we're experiencing that, and that's certainly beneficial from a longer-term perspective."

JOSEPH LIRO, CHIEF ECONOMIST, CIBC WOOD GUNDY SECURITIES CORP: "It looks like the overall number is down because of the sharp drop in energy prices, a bigger-than-expected drop in food prices. In the core goods, computer prices were down over 4.0 percent.

Asked if the report would make the Federal Reserve less likely to raise interest rates next week, Liro said "on the margin, yes. But I still think they're going to go. I don't think it's the on-the-ground inflation news that they're reacting to."
KEVIN FLANAGAN, VICE PRESIDENT AND MONEY MARKET ECONOMIST, DEAN WITTER REYNOLDS INC: "It's certainly better than what investors had anticipated. But a lot of good news has already been factored in.
"We've yet to see any price pressures on the wholesale level. It will have to enter into discussions at the Fed."

PATRICK DIMICK, TREASURY STRATEGIST, UBS SECURITIES: "These are terrific numbers for the bond market. The only thing we have to keep in mind is that the Fed and the market are going to be focused on demand side data. We'll have to keep that in mind as the market is surging to its highs here.
"The headline statistic is spectacular for bonds, but what is really helpful is the year-over-year readings on core crudes and core intermediates.

"In summarizing the pipeline pressures -- lots of relief to steady and that reinforces the good news in the headline. But I caution this is not a demand side statistic and needs to be relegated to secondary status."
